paragraphs.source_en: Muzzolini (1995a) notices the similar evolution in the Sahara as well, and he claims that the artistic styles representing the bow are older than the styles with other types of weapon. However, the bow is present in the Bubaline engravings, in the Round Head paintings and also in the Pastoral engravings and paintings, which indicates that these three styles are older than the Caballine and Cameline styles, but it does not determine the absolute chronology of the earliest rock art.

paragraphs.source_en: No bow has been found in excavations in the study area but arrow heads are present within Epipalaeolithic levels (Aumassip 1980-1; Barich 1987). Muzzolini (1995a) notes that in paintings the bow is very frequent in the Round Head style and that it is rarer in the Pastoral style. He considers the Round Head and Pastoral styles as contemporaneous but the decreasing quantity of the bow in the Pastoral style may indicate the actual relative chronology of these two style-periods.
